title: observability-api-requestid-trace-structured-logs-metrics-openai-compat
author: Ethan Wang
release_notes: Adds request-id and trace propagation to API surface, structured logs with trace/request fields, and per-endpoint metrics tags. Backwards-compatible; toggle via feature flag. Improves observability for streaming and function-calling flows.
description: Motivation: we need end-to-end observability on the public API surface (hosted + OpenAI-compatible endpoints) to reliably correlate user requests across gateway, streaming runtime, and downstream workers. This PR implements request-id propagation, trace id embedding into structured logs, and per-endpoint metrics tags so cost/latency can be attributed to routes and model variants. Changes are backward compatible and gated by a rollout flag. Summary of changes: - New request_id middleware that accepts and normalizes incoming request headers (x-request-id, openai-request-id, x-redwood-request-id) and injects a canonical request_id into context. - Trace propagation: wire trace/span ids through HTTP, streaming (SSE/websocket/protocol-specific frames), and internal RPCs so logs and metrics can be correlated across services. - Structured logs: updated logger to emit JSON fields (request_id, trace_id, route, model, function_call_id when present). Maintains plain-text log formatting as controlled by config. - Per-endpoint metrics tags: metrics incremented with tags route=<route>, model=<model> and this is available for per-tenant aggregation. - OpenAI compatibility: accept legacy OpenAI headers and expose openai-request-id in responses for compatibility. - Streaming + function-calling: ensure in-stream events (delta tokens, function call start/complete/error) include request_id and trace_id in metadata frames so observability tools can stitch partial/streamed outputs back to a single request. - Tests and docs: integration tests for streaming and function-calling flows, unit tests for middleware, and updated observability docs and runbook. Migration/rollout plan: 1) Feature-flagged behind config:observability.api_propagation_enabled=false by default. 2) Canary rollout to 10% of traffic with additional logging and sampling rates adjusted to avoid metrics explosion. 3) Monitor latency impact, cardinality on metrics, and logging volume with retention limits; revert if >3% P50 latency regression or >20% increase in logging cost. Checklist: - [x] Middleware + propagation across HTTP and streaming - [x] Structured logger updates - [x] Per-endpoint metrics tagging - [x] OpenAI header compatibility - [x] Integration tests for streaming + function-calls - [x] Docs and runbook updates - [x] Canary rollout plan and feature flagging Performance notes: microbenchmarks show ~0.2ms median added latency for simple echo endpoints and negligible CPU overhead for low sampling. High-throughput paths use sampling for full structured payloads. Related: ENG-4521 (observability roadmap), ENG-4590 (streaming stability improvements).

notes_for_ops: Feature flag: observability.api_propagation_enabled. To enable canary: set observability.canary.percent=10 and observability.logging.sample_rate=0.1. Watch metrics: telemetry.requests.tag_cardinality, logs.ingress_bytes, latency.p50/90. Run runbooks/observability/trace-propagation.md for troubleshooting.
changelog_entry: Observability: request-id + trace propagation on API surface, structured logs with request_id/trace_id, per-endpoint metrics tags, and OpenAI header compatibility for request ids. Backwards-compatible and feature-flagged; canary rollout recommended.
notes_for_sdk_teams: SDKs should continue to send any existing request-id header. New behavior: if SDK sends openai-request-id it will be honored and echoed; otherwise server will generate and return X-Request-Id. SDKs may optionally surface the returned request id to users for debugging.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover middleware and header normalization. Integration tests exercise HTTP + websocket + SSE streaming flows including function-calling start/complete/error events and assert request_id/trace_id propagation. Performance microbenchmarks in scripts/perf showed median added latency ~0.2ms. Observability sampling prevents excessive cardinality in production tests.
rollback_plan: Disable observability.api_propagation_enabled or rollback the config to previous commit. For immediate mitigation, set observability.logging.sample_rate=0 to stop structured payload emission. Ops runbook contains steps to revert config and purge any high-cardinality metrics tags.
external_impacts: Customers using OpenAI-compatible SDKs will see 'openai-request-id' echoed in responses when present. No breaking API changes. Internal metrics dashboards will show new tags which consumers should update to include route/model when slicing latency/cost reports.
